trust_decision.summary: CP navigation page endpoints trust the session user's 'view' permission on the site-scoped nav tree and on each referenced entry; the decision is made ad hoc inside each controller action via $this->authorize(), so any route that returns nav-page entry data without calling it returns restricted entries.

landing_point.why: the only CP place that returns a nav page's merged entry values and originValues to the page editor; a reader of 'navigation endpoint discloses restricted entries' looks at the nav page editor first

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The shared tree transformer is infrastructure that also serves the collection tree; the report is about the navigation page-editor endpoints, the nav screen already authorizes view on the nav, and nav-level permission is not entry-level permission, so the builder looks like the wrong place to fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Nav pages that are plain URL/text links have no entry at all; an unconditional entry authorization (or authorizing a null entry) turns every plain nav link into a 403, so the entry check must stay inside the 'if ($entry = $page->entry())' branch. An existing test covers this shape (tests/Feature/Navigation/CreateNavigationPageTest.php:53-84).

O6_input_shapes: site query parameter selecting the site-scoped nav tree on create and edit ($nav->in($request->site))
entry query parameter on create: a new page created from an existing entry id
{edit} page id on edit: the entry comes from the stored tree branch, not from the request
POST pages/update body: nav handle only, no site parameter and no entry id
type=url vs type=entry in the update body; the fix authorizes the nav for both and never checks the entry for type=entry

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /cp/navigation/{nav}/tree returns the whole nav tree with entry_title, entry status, entry redirect and entry url per referenced entry, and has no authorization call at all
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The nav show screen already authorizes view on the site-scoped nav (src/Http/Controllers/CP/Navigation/NavigationController.php:85), so this looks like a data source for an already-guarded screen rather than a public entry point; the report named the page editor.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: adjacent file in the same controller directory

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PATCH /cp/navigation/{nav}/tree authorizes 'edit' on the tree but accepts arbitrary 'entry' ids in submitted branches (src/Http/Controllers/CP/Navigation/NavigationTreeController.php:79) and never checks entry view
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a write/validation endpoint, not a disclosure route; the advisory is about reading restricted entries.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the tree index, ~15 lines below

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /cp/collections/{collection}/tree returns the same entry-derived payload through the same transformer with no authorization call
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different feature: the advisory names navigation, and the collection tree belongs to the collections screens.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /api/navs/{nav}/tree returns the nav tree over the public REST API with no per-entry restriction (TreeResource default query only filters status published)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The public read API is gated by config/ResourceAuthorizer and has no CP user, so CP role permissions do not apply to it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate transport and namespace (src/Http/Controllers/API plus src/Http/Resources/API)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-entry view filter (or a sibling 'viewable' key next to can_delete) in the shared controller transformer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the transformer already consults the policy for delete on the very same entry one line away, so a maintainer adding entry permission handling there is natural

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a build() path variant for non-nav structures (taxonomies/collections) that reuses the same entry resolution without any permission filter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: build() is the shared entry point for the Antlers tag, GraphQL structure type and both tree controllers, so a new caller inherits the same unprotected payload

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a page preview or 'existing page' action that extracts values for an entry without the two authorize calls
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: create and edit both duplicate the same extract-then-origin-values shape, so a third copy for preview is a one-method addition a maintainer would plausibly write

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second transport (API) rendering the nav tree where per-entry visibility must be applied through the query argument
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the resource already takes a nullable query and the collection tree controller passes one while the nav tree controller does not

O9_family: missing authorization / improper access control (CWE-862, CWE-639)

O10_build.toolchain: Composer (Laravel 12 / orchestra/testbench 10, PHPUnit ^10.5|^11.5), phpunit.xml.dist with sqlite :memory:

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add $this->authorize('view', $nav) to create, edit and update and stop, without the per-entry check and without noticing that update checks the whole nav instead of the site-scoped tree.

out_of_scope_notes: The nav tree update route also lets an edit-nav-only user write arbitrary entry ids into a navigation, which is a write-side sibling but not the advisory's disclosure property.
